findings.note: Residual sh/ps1 divergence and conformance fail-open on `"upgrade_reasons": {}`. The sh twin uses `reasons = entry.get("upgrade_reasons") or []`, and an empty JSON object is FALSY in Python, so `{}` is treated as absent: `{"capabilities":[{"id":"a","eligible":true,"upgrade_reasons":{}}]}` exits 0/`lite-eligible`. The ps1 twin's `Test-PythonFalsy` (check-risk-upgrade.ps1:60) returns $false for a PSCustomObject (it tests only null/bool/string/array/numeric), so the same fragment falls into the `-isnot [array]` branch and exits 2 via Write-FragmentInvalid. Same input, two verdicts across runtimes. The staged policy doc (human-copy/plugins/sdd-lite/references/risk-upgrade-policy.md, `Deterministic contract` bullet) pins the falsy set as exactly `false`, `0`, `""`, `[]`, `null` and requires exit 2 for any `upgrade_reasons` that is `present, truthy and not an array` -- `{}` is not in that falsy set, so the sh twin violates its own delivered contract. This is precisely the class the 2026-08-28 RT-20260828-001 amendment (`an eligible:true entry carrying a malformed value was silently accepted (exit 0, lite-eligible)`) and the twin-parity sweep claim to have closed; no fixture in TEST-013v..013aj covers `{}`.

GREEN evidence predates the code and suite under review. Both green artifacts are captured 2026-08-25 at HEAD 4905c13143ca29e103d6b35130754f68cb83dc14 (this log's own header line 1; verification/T-002.green.log:2 same HEAD) and record `Results: 61 passed` for the fail-closed suite. The bundled CURRENT worktree suite runs 67 assertions -- it adds TEST-013ag/ah (2 assertions each via assert_fragment_invalid) and TEST-013ai/aj (1 each) -- and both staged scripts now carry the 2026-08-28 `amended 2b` rewrite. T-002.contract.json therefore names, as `green_evidence` for the two required checks unit-tests and acceptance-tests, a log that exercises neither the current SUT nor AC-027's amended fixtures. investigation.md's closing update asserts a post-fix green run at `identical tallies`, but no such log is in the bundle and `identical tallies` cannot be true across a 61->67 assertion change; a narrative claim is not the evidence artifact the contract cites.

Two REQUIRED checks are recorded `passes: false`, so the default-FAIL verification contract does not certify this task. `regression` (line 71) is false and its own named evidence (verification/qg/shared/regression.log) concludes `VERDICT: passes stays FALSE` with `Two real, unwaived, non-designed-red suites fail`. `placeholder-scan` (line 94) is false and its evidence ends `Placeholder scan FAILED (5 finding(s)) ... exit: 1` against CHANGELOG.md -- a file T-002 declares as one of its own Outputs -- with no quality-gate report on record carrying the human acceptance the scanner's own message requires. The pre-existence proof for the 5 findings is present and credible, but it is an argument for a human waiver, not a waiver.

AC-027's companion clause requires pinning present-but-falsy `upgrade_reasons` (`false`/`0`/`""`/`[]`/`null`) as treated-absent on both runtimes. TEST-013ai pins only `false` and TEST-013aj only `0`; `[]` is covered indirectly by TEST-014b and an absent key by TEST-014a, but the empty string and JSON `null` have no assertion in either twin. Both happen to behave correctly today, so this is a coverage gap rather than a defect -- but it is the same untested-corner shape that let `{}` diverge.

The RED log contains no TEST-007 capture, so the byte-identical-legacy-path contract (AC-007, 16 assertions) has red_evidence in name only. The implementation report concedes the hole and explains it correctly -- under the `point the SUT at the live script` mechanism this log used, a TEST-007 red is structurally unobtainable because live-vs-live is trivially byte-identical -- and declines to manufacture one now. Accepted as disclosed, recorded because the contract's red_evidence field points at this file for a check it does not exercise.
